blocks.content: Connect Grafana Cloud to your existing private Prometheus server with Private Data Source Connect (PDC). You will create a network in Grafana, run an agent on your network, and test a Prometheus data source.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.content: You need permission to add data sources and manage PDC networks and signing tokens, your private Prometheus URL and any credentials, and a Docker host on the private network that can reach Prometheus. If you are returning to an unfinished setup, check which network and data source you already created before adding duplicates.
Start in the Grafana Cloud UI where you manage private networks.

blocks.tooltip: Open the page where Grafana manages private connections.
blocks.content: Open **Private data source connect** to set up the route from Grafana Cloud to your private network.
This page is where you create and manage the private network used by your data source.
Create a private network and signing token in Grafana, then run the generated Docker command on your network.

blocks.title: Create a network and connect an agent

blocks.content: Create the private network `my-prometheus-network`.

steps.tooltip: Start configuring a route into your private network.
steps.description: Click **Add new network** to create a connection for your Prometheus server.

steps.tooltip: Use a recognizable name for the route you will select later.
steps.description: Name the private network `my-prometheus-network` so you can recognize it when configuring the data source.

steps.tooltip: Create the network and open its setup instructions.
steps.description: Click **Add** to create the network and open its configuration.

blocks.tooltip: Display the instructions for deploying on your Docker host.
blocks.content: Choose **Running the PDC Agent Docker image** to display the Docker setup instructions.

blocks.tooltip: Give the credential a name that identifies its purpose.
blocks.content: Name the signing token `my-prometheus-pdc-token` so you can identify its purpose later.
Create your signing token, then deploy the agent on your private network.

steps.tooltip: Review the expiration and create the credential yourself.
steps.description: Review the token expiration in Grafana, then click **Create token** yourself. Keep the generated credential in the setup UI; do not paste it into this guide or chat.

steps.reftarget: h5:contains("Deploy the PDC agent on your private network")
steps.tooltip: Run the generated command on a host that can reach your private endpoint.
steps.description: On your own Docker host inside the private network, run the agent command generated by Grafana. Use a host whose agent can reach your Prometheus endpoint, and leave the agent running. Grafana provides the command; you run it in your own terminal. Highlighting these instructions does not deploy the agent.

blocks.tooltip: Confirm that at least one agent is connected before continuing.
blocks.content: Click **Test agent connection** and wait for at least one connected agent. If none connects, check that the agent is running and follow the setup UI before continuing.
The agent connection checks the route to Grafana Cloud; the next steps check whether Prometheus is reachable through it.

blocks.title: Check the agent before moving on
blocks.content: Continue only when your new network reports at least one connected agent. This confirms the agent connection, but you still need to configure and test the Prometheus data source.
Set the private endpoint, authentication, and PDC network, then test the Prometheus API.

blocks.tooltip: Open the catalog to add your private endpoint.
blocks.content: With an agent connected, open **Add data source** to configure Prometheus.

blocks.tooltip: Create a data source for querying your existing server.
blocks.content: Select **Prometheus** to create the data source.
Name the data source `my-private-prometheus`.

steps.tooltip: Enable editing so you can identify this data source later.
steps.description: Click **Edit title** to give this data source a recognizable name.

steps.tooltip: Use this name for the configuration and its final verification.

blocks.tooltip: Enter the HTTP or HTTPS address reachable from your agent.
blocks.content: Enter your private Prometheus server URL under **Connection**, beginning with `http://` or `https://`. Use the address reachable from the PDC agent, including its port when needed.

blocks.tooltip: Configure the method your endpoint requires and enter credentials directly in Grafana.
blocks.content: Choose the authentication method your endpoint requires and enter any credentials directly in Grafana. Select **No Authentication** only if your endpoint requires no credentials. PDC provides network access; your endpoint may still require authentication.

blocks.tooltip: Route queries through the network you created earlier.
blocks.content: Select `my-prometheus-network` under **Private data source connect** to route this data source through the agent you connected.

blocks.tooltip: Confirm that Grafana can query the private endpoint through the connected agent.
blocks.content: Click **Save & test** and wait for **Successfully queried the Prometheus API**. A connected PDC agent alone does not confirm this data source can query Prometheus.
A successful Prometheus API check confirms the configured data source can query your private endpoint through PDC.

blocks.title: If Save & test fails
blocks.content: Confirm the selected PDC network has a connected agent, then check that the Prometheus URL is reachable from that agent and that endpoint authentication is correct. Run **Save & test** again after correcting the configuration.
